name: Clockwork Resin
detail: Dry wooden pulses climb two octaves. Hold a minor chord for a steady sixteenth-note pattern.

name: Descending Glass
detail: Clear harmonic droplets fall through two octaves, with a spacious quarter-note echo.

name: Pinwheel Orchard
detail: Rounded triangle notes travel up and down. Open voicings make a gentle eighth-note ostinato.

name: Random Fireflies
detail: Bright, short sparks choose random chord tones over three octaves. Hold three or four notes.

name: Octave Engine
detail: A gritty low pulse alternates octaves. Try a single held note for a driving bass sequence.

name: Cathedral Steps
detail: Slow quarter-note chimes rise above a soft sustained octave. Let a chord settle for several seconds.

name: Circuit Sprint
detail: A tight saw sequence races in thirty-second notes. Small chords keep the pattern focused.

name: Velvet Sequence
detail: Soft filtered eighth notes with long gates and subtle stereo movement, suited to relaxed chord changes.

name: Twin Orbits
detail: Two layers move in opposite directions at different rates. Hold a triad to hear their interlocking patterns.

name: Neon Ladder
detail: Bright, detuned saw notes climb three octaves with a resonant opening on every step.

name: Radio Snow
detail: A band-pass wash of filtered noise and faint harmonics. Sustain a low chord and let the filter wander.

name: Deep Observatory
detail: Low sine foundations and distant high harmonics drift slowly across the stereo field.

name: Broken Neon
detail: A square-wave filter pulse chops an edgy sustained tone. Sparse notes reveal the abrupt movement.

name: Wind Through Wire
detail: Breathy high-pass harmonics with a slow tremolo. Play above middle C for an airy, fragile shimmer.

name: Glass Tectonics
detail: Two harmonic layers a fifth apart bend gently against each other. Hold open intervals for slow beating.

name: Dust Carousel
detail: A grainy harmonic bed turns through a slow pan cycle while its filter rises and falls.

name: Submerged Choir
detail: Dark pulse and triangle layers form a hollow, submerged ensemble. Use low, widely spaced chords.

name: Random Lanterns
detail: Random filter positions reveal different overtones in a sustained harmonic drone.

name: Solar Static
detail: A bright noise halo sits above a warm saw foundation. Build slowly with suspended chords.

name: Heartbeat Nebula
detail: A soft sine pulse beats beneath a long harmonic cloud. Hold a single note or simple fifth.

name: Chapel Air
detail: Gentle fundamental and octave ranks with a little air. Sustained triads suit this quiet chapel tone.

name: Gospel Ember
detail: A full, slightly driven registration with a short upper percussion layer. Play rhythmic gospel chords.

name: Reed Arcade
detail: Bright pulse reeds evoke a compact transistor organ. Short chords and single-note melodies cut clearly.

name: Flute Gallery
detail: Pure, rounded flute stops at the fundamental and two octaves. A light touch gives a small chamber sound.

name: Fifth Registration
detail: An exposed twelfth adds a hollow, woody edge to a sine-based registration. Try open fifths or modal lines.

name: Rotating Amber
detail: A mellow organ with animated pan, light pitch motion, and chorus for a swirling stereo character.

name: Percussion Trio
detail: A compact fundamental-and-octave organ with a bright decaying attack. Repeated staccato chords emphasize the percussion.

name: Low Nave
detail: Deep pedal tones support a restrained middle rank. Play slowly in the middle register for a heavy, solemn sound.

name: Festival Pipes
detail: Four bright ranks build a broad ceremonial organ. Use simple voicings and leave room for the reverberation.

name: Night Drawbars
detail: A dark, intimate organ with gentle tremolo and a soft lower octave. Best for quiet jazz voicings.

name: Sunroom Strings
detail: Two warm saw ensembles open gradually, with restrained vibrato. Sustain broad chords for a vintage string-machine color.

name: Cinema Bow
detail: A slow string swell with a quiet octave canopy. Hold each chord to hear the upper layer bloom.

name: Staccato Silk
detail: Short saw-and-triangle string stabs with a brisk decay. Play detached chords or repeated ostinatos.

name: Muted Boulevard
detail: A soft, nasal synthetic brass ensemble with a rounded attack. Close jazz chords bring out its muted character.

name: Brass Arrival
detail: A bold two-layer saw brass with an opening filter attack. Try short, accented major chords.

name: French Circuit
detail: Triangle and saw layers produce a mellow, rounded horn-like swell. Melodies in the middle register sound most natural.

name: Disco Section
detail: Bright octave strings with a quick bow and wide chorus. Rhythmic triads fit its energetic vintage tone.

name: Cello Circuit
detail: A dark lower-octave saw body with a little bow noise and gentle vibrato. Play single lines near middle C.

name: Violet Chamber
detail: A restrained ensemble of midrange strings and a soft lower voice. Smaller voicings keep it intimate.

name: Fanfarer
detail: A bright, brassy octave stack with a firm attack and short room. Play clean, separated fanfare phrases.

name: Anchor / Mist
detail: Below middle C: rounded sub bass. From middle C: a slow, warm pad. Keep bass notes detached while the pad blooms.

name: Pluck / Lantern
detail: Below middle C: a woody plucked bass. From middle C: bright harmonic keys with a short echo.

name: Organ / Reed
detail: Below middle C: a full sine-organ foundation. From middle C: a nasal pulse lead for two-hand melodies.

name: Rubber / Rain
detail: Below middle C: a resonant rubber bass. From middle C: an eighth-note triangle arpeggio over two octaves.

name: Cello / Glass
detail: Below middle C: a warm bowed synth voice. From middle C: clear bell-like harmonic keys. Let low notes sustain.

name: Pulse / Brass
detail: Below middle C: tight driven pulse bass. From middle C: a bright synthetic brass section for rhythmic chords.

name: Drone / Fireflies
detail: Below middle C: a slow dark drone. From middle C: short random sixteenth-note sparks. Hold one low note beneath an upper chord.

name: Round / Ribbon
detail: Below middle C: a dry, round triangle bass. From middle C: a singing detuned saw lead with light vibrato.

name: Mallet / Halo
detail: Below middle C: a soft triangle mallet. From middle C: a wide, high-pass shimmer. Use left-hand arpeggios beneath sustained chords.

name: Funk / Chapel
detail: Below middle C: a snappy filter bass. From middle C: a soft two-rank organ. Try syncopated bass under sustained right-hand chords.
